This game is so much fun! I recently got steam and downloaded it here, making it the third device I have this game on! I have over 500 hours in this game total. An absolute masterpiece.
I have 112%ed this game twice and am now seeking to get all achievements. That shows how much I love this game no matter the platform (get it)
This practically free game has stunning visuals, unique combat, and a master crafted soundtrack.
It all feels alive- each step you take, bush you brush, enemy you defeat- everything reacts and moves around you.
This has been my favourite game since long before this moment- don't think I'm lying or being hasty, because despite only having 100 minutes on this account, I have hundreds of hours on both my nintendo switch and my other account on steam.
Team Cherry has created not just a silly game about bugs with a dark backstory- no. They have crafted this world. On the surface, it's a difficult soulslike. On the inside, each character has a past, a life, each little pixel being intended, planned, precise. Team Cherry has spared no expense of their time and effort to detail everything you see in the vast, open world around you.
There is struggle to every encounter.
Hardship to every boss...
But it's addicting. And at the end of it all, when you've finally mastered your foe, you slay them.
In that moment you feel a rush of joy and relief and pride (i swear hollow knight isn't a drug)
You just must play this game.
10/10

while the game isn't quite as good as people have told you it is, it's still indubitably fantastic through a combination of a vibrant, visually captivating world, strong platforming, a strong soundtrack and enjoyable combat... though that last bit can be a bit marred by how absurdly powerful spells are, which allow the player to severely trivialize much of the harder fights in the game. even with them in mind, the fast paced boss fights manage to stay fairly interesting, which is honestly impressive considering how ridiculously good shriek and dive both are

my gripes with the game (beyond the spells being so strong and comparatively easier to build around, making the game be significantly centered around them compared to the nail and nail arts) mostly extend to backtracking being boring (being in an area for the first time is cool and exciting. being in it the second time is a little uninteresting. having to traverse it yet again as a stepping stone for your actually wanted destination is eye-rolling), as well as the sluggishness of the early game (while pogoing on spikes is flashy and interesting and quite easily the most interesting part of the game's platforming it's also fairly slow to be stuck without dash, double jump or wallclimb, and once all these tools are acquired the game goes from a bit slow to extremely fun in terms of its platforming, to the point where it makes the backtracking a bit more tolerable, to the game's credit).

all in all, it's good. it's strong. it's fun. it's a bit strange that this game blew up as hard as it did, to me at least, but it's at least not hard to see why; despite its flaws and my gripes with the game it would just be disingenuous of me to not recommend it, game's great.

The biggest stumbling block for most people is runbacks, which are not my personal favorite but the game is easy enough that it didn't ruin the experience for me. I first was introduced to this game through art made by the community. Seeing the numerous art pieces intrigued me to learn about the lore of the game itself. Before I knew it, I purchased it, began the first save file, and the rest is history. I immediately enjoyed the game through its art style and layout overall, figuring out the lore while fighting a bunch of bugs and bosses. Whenever I first read reviews of how the game is difficult, I won't lie, it is form the new creatures to navigating the terranium. I thought about giving up at times when it took me forever to defeat the FALSE KNIGHT! However, I took my time, analyzed the patterns, and before I knew it, I defeated the first boss. It took more attempts than I like to admit (about 15...) but I felt accomplished and capable of going through the rest of the game. As I progressed I would say the mantis sisters in Mantis City took me the longest so far (36 TIMES) and I have no idea how many times I lost SO MUCH GEO to simple creatures, but the game made me push through. Right now I'm navigating through the City of Tears and I am shaking in my boots. However, I know if I take my time and pay attention to the environment, I know will conquer. If there is one theme this game expresses early on is the importance of patience and persistence. To anyone who is starting out, just know that you have what it takes to explore and defeat those enemies! I wish you and I luck throughout the playthrough.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Longtime players describe the combat as tough but fair, highlighting the standout audio and hand-drawn visuals while acknowledging that the early stages require patience before the game truly opens up.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the early game can feel slow or difficult to get into before acquiring movement abilities and maps.

citations.review_text:
Gameplay — 10/10

Hollow Knight’s controls are simple, responsive and extremely precise. Movement initially feels limited, but the game gradually introduces abilities that completely change how you explore and approach combat.

The combat system is easy to understand but difficult to master. Attacks, spells, healing and movement all need to be carefully timed, especially during harder boss fights. The game rarely feels unfair, as most deaths come from mistimed attacks, poor positioning or failing to learn an enemy’s patterns.

The only major issue is that the early game can feel slow before several important movement abilities are unlocked.

Story and Lore — 10/10

The story is told indirectly through environmental details, item descriptions, NPC dialogue and optional discoveries. Very little is directly explained, which fits the mysterious atmosphere of Hallownest but can also make the main plot difficult to understand during a first playthrough.

The lore surrounding the kingdom, the infection and its characters is incredibly detailed. Even minor NPCs and optional areas often contribute something meaningful to the world.

Understanding everything will likely require additional playthroughs, careful exploration or a few lore videos. However, the mystery is one of the game’s greatest strengths and gives players a reason to examine every area closely.

Environment, Visuals and Atmosphere — 10/10

Hollow Knight’s hand-drawn art style still looks exceptional. Every major area has its own visual identity, atmosphere and colour palette, making most locations instantly recognisable.

Hallownest feels abandoned without feeling empty. Background creatures, environmental animations and small visual details make the world feel like it existed long before the player arrived.

The atmosphere constantly shifts between peaceful, unsettling and tragic. Even with its simple visual style, the game creates a stronger sense of place than many significantly larger games.

The game also has a really friendly, supportive community and great modding support. I would easily recommend it to everyone. Team Cherry really earned a place in my heart with this game. Of course, the beginning can be challenging without a map or a clear direction—but hey, you’re playing a Metroidvania, all of this is part of your Hollow Knight experience.
To sum it up: a great single-player game you can try at any skill level. 
(Yes, you will die—but you’ll learn.)

Review in a nutshell: 
ABSOLUTE MASTERPIECE

Review outside of a nutshell:
I try to avoid spoilers. I was initially hesitant to buy this game because I don't really like hard games. Whenever there are difficulty options, I chose medium. However, I liked the artstyle, so when it was on sale, I thought I give it a go. In hindsight I feel a bit like a thief because the amount of game you get for the regular price is ridiculously huge.

The artstyle is really beautiful and it also makes it easy to see what is going on on the screen. As someone with a visual impairment, this is quite important to me.
The soundtrack is also something that blew me away right from the start. In my opinion, Christopher larkin is in the same league as John Williams.

Let's get to the gameplay. The death mechanic seemed intimidating at first, but even if you die before retrieving your currency, you will quickly notice, that geo is not really hard to find.
The toughest bosses are also optional. So you can reach the game's ending even if you avoid the hardest challenges. But once the game finally gets you, you won't want to avoid them, because there are some really fun and amazing boss fights.

The atmosphere and the world that Team Cherry has created, are really breathtaking. As you progress, you meet quirky characters, uncover more bits of the lore and discover numerous secrets in hidden areas. This was my first metroidvania and I found out that I actually like that part. 

However, the game has some flaws. Some secrets are simply impossible to find, without looking them up online. You can not tell me, that there are people who find the path of pain or the eternal ordeal organically. Some secrets are also hidden e bit too well. for example the white defender or the junk pit. For the amount of gameplay that is locked in there, you probably don't want to miss it. Another problem for me were 2-3 boss fights where some attacks were yellow/orange and so was the background.
